analysis: The only change in this file (QwenVLMTargetExtractionTests.swift, head lines ~335-366) is a new unit test, endOfPromptBoundaryRequiresDensePagedSSD. It checks EngineV2Factory.demandedLatestCheckpointMinimumTokens and demandedCaptureBoundaryMinimumTokens against a dense/MoE Qwen target, paged/contiguous backend and SSD hybrid checkpoint store fixtures. The base units contain only the unchanged surrounding test file, with no production code. The change is test-only and touches no production gate, key handling, TTL, lookup-tag derivation, disk budget or coordinator interface. It exercises an existing SSD cache configuration path rather than altering it, so I found no regression against T-041 or TB-007. The new test cleans up its fixtures through defer { fixture.remove() } and store.close(). The patch excerpt is truncated (patch_excerpt_complete=false), so I could not see the tail of the new test, which creates a contiguous fixture. The production counterpart (demandedLatestCheckpointMinimumTokens in EngineV2Factory) is not supplied here. A later pass should check that it keeps the same SSD per-donation gating and the min-effective-token floor, and that end-of-prompt boundary captures do not widen the at-rest surface described in T-041. This is a coverage limit, not evidence of a defect.
